## Isotropic viscosity and heat conduction (`forcing/diffusion`) {#sec-ch09-viscosity}

### Summary

The diffusion module is snapy's only closure for sub-grid momentum and heat transport: constant isotropic
coefficients, optionally shaped in $x_1$ (@sec-ch09-x1profile). With the default `dynamic: false`, `nu_iso`[^rg-8453b354c365] is a
kinematic viscosity $\nu$ [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$] multiplied by the face density, and `kappa_iso`[^rg-c881080d630d] a thermal
diffusivity $\kappa$[^rg-e72046dad063] [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$] multiplied by the face volumetric heat capacity $\rho c_v$. With
`dynamic: true` the two numbers are a dynamic viscosity $\mu$[^rg-6149e61825cb] [$\mathrm{Pa\,s}$] and a conductivity, still written
$\kappa$ but in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ (appendix A, notation group 8), and no density enters. The heat flux acts on the
temperature, not on the potential temperature, so a resting adiabatic column, which is neutrally stable, is heated
in the interior and at the walls (Limits). This section is the operator of Cartesian grids; on the gnomonic cubed
sphere the same keys select the operator of @sec-ch09-csdiffusion.

For numerical diffusion/dissipation, see the Roe solver's fallback to the local Lax–Friedrichs flux in @sec-ch04-roe:
its dissipative term is half the largest left/right signal speed times the conserved-state jump
({{< code src/riemann/roe_impl.h roe_impl >}}). This is separate from the configured physical viscosity here.
The task map (@sec-appg) explicitly states: **Not provided:** no list of numerical dissipation and no
physical-vs-numerical split; that missing inventory is not supplied by this physical-diffusion section.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Adds the Newtonian viscous stress, its work, and a Fourier heat flux as face fluxes whose divergence
enters the stage increment; @eq-ch09-viscosity-flux.

**Data.** In: cell velocity, temperature and diffusion coefficients; out: momentum and energy tendencies from face fluxes.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, third in the forcing loop; its time-step bound joins the hyperbolic one.

**Activation.** `forcing/diffusion: {nu_iso, kappa_iso, dynamic, nu_scale_x1, kappa_scale_x1, temperature_inner, temperature_outer}`; defaults 0, 0,
`false`, none, none, 0, 0. Acts only through a positive coefficient. Runs on a `cartesian` grid (cubed sphere: @sec-ch09-csdiffusion);
$n_{\mathrm{ghost}}\ge2$ for viscosity, and a positive reference $c_v$[^rg-0527910bf49b] for conduction.

**Guarantee / limits.** Momentum and total energy conserved; second order in the interior, first order in the wall
normal-stress kernel; conduction acts on $T$, not on the potential temperature.

**Evidence.** Report checks and the ctest run at the pin are listed in the Tests layer.
:::

**Data details.** In: the cell-centre velocity $\mathbf v$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$], temperature $T$ [$\mathrm{K}$],
density $\rho$ and mixture $c_v$ of the stage, ghosts included ($n_{\mathrm{ghost}}\ge2$ for viscosity), and the
coefficients `nu_iso`, `kappa_iso` [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$, or $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ with
`dynamic: true`]. Out: face fluxes of momentum [$\mathrm{Pa}$] and energy [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$] on every active
direction, and their divergence in the momentum and energy rows. Check cases: transverse and normal modes at
$n_1 = 64$, a random shear at $n_1 = 48$, a resting dry adiabat at $n_1$[^rg-ca98cd88ebb0] = 64, 128, 256.

**Evidence details.** Tests: a transverse $v_2=x_1^2$ gives the uniform viscous Laplacian,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.transverse_velocity_uses_viscous_laplacian >}} ($10^{-5}$); a sine mode
decays as $e^{-\nu t}$ over 100 steps, {{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.viscous_sine_mode_matches_analytic_decay >}}
($3\times10^{-4}$); the bound uses the larger coefficient,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.timestep_uses_largest_diffusivity >}} ($10^{-12}$); a prescribed wall
temperature keeps a linear profile at rest and injects the expected heat,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp DeviceTest.cartesian_fixed_temperature_preserves_linear_conduction >}} ($10^{-9}$);
these ctests pass at the pin.[^vis-ctest] Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/viscosity_check.py`, output `viscosity_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C8]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical [^env-viscosity].

Local symbols: $\boldsymbol\Pi$ [Pa] the viscous stress tensor ($\tau$[^rg-d9c30f993349] is a named relaxation
time in appendix A); $F^{(m_b)}_a$ [Pa] and $F^{(E)}_a$ [W m$^{-2}$] the momentum and energy fluxes through a face normal to
$x_a$; $\delta_{ab}$ the Kronecker delta; $n_{\mathrm{dim}}$ the number of active directions; $\Delta x_{\min}$ [m] the smallest
active cell width; $K_{\Delta t}$ [m$^2$ s$^{-1}$] the coefficient of the time-step bound; $G$ [-] the forward-Euler
amplification of the checkerboard mode; $\varsigma_{\max}$ the largest value of an $x_1$ profile (@sec-ch09-x1profile).
$\nu$, $\mu$, $\kappa$, $c_v$, $c_{p,\mathrm d}$, $c_{v,\mathrm d}$, $R_{\mathrm d}$[^rg-520b6f3f3b47], $g_1$[^rg-2608062c5408], $h$, $\vartheta$[^rg-90ec1bf7716b], $\lambda_w$[^rg-778cd93f3ca5] and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

The module adds its own time-step bound, $\Delta t\le \Delta x_{\min}^2/(2n_{\mathrm{dim}}K_{\Delta t})$, with $\Delta x_{\min}$ the smallest cell width over the active directions, which the solver takes
together with the hyperbolic bound before the Courant factor is applied (@sec-ch07-cfl). The YAML parser refuses
the keys `K` and `type`. Two keys, `temperature_inner`[^rg-a3880ab85786] and `temperature_outer`[^rg-900e6f628025], replace the conductive flux through a
reflecting $x_1$ wall by the flux to a prescribed wall temperature (Numerical method); 0, the default, leaves the
wall insulating. The keys `wall_velocity`[^rg-78156b20840f] and `implicit_radial` act only on the cubed sphere.

### Derivation

All quantities in this layer are per unit volume; $h$ is the cell width, uniform in $x_2$ and $x_3$, and in $x_1$
unless $x_1$ is stretched (`geometry/x1f` or `cells/x1rat`), where the widths $h_i$[^rg-83f672728ba8] [m] vary from cell to cell (this operator
runs on Cartesian grids only; the module refuses every grid but Cartesian and the cubed sphere). Units: $\mathbf v$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$], $T$ [$\mathrm{K}$], momentum fluxes
[$\mathrm{Pa}$], energy fluxes [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$].

#### Continuous fluxes

The Newtonian stress for a fluid with no bulk viscosity is
$\boldsymbol\Pi = \mu[\nabla\mathbf v + (\nabla\mathbf v)^{\mathsf T} - \tfrac23(\nabla\cdot\mathbf v)\mathsf I]$, and
the momentum and energy equations gain $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol\Pi$ and $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\Pi\cdot\mathbf v)$
plus the divergence of the Fourier heat flux, a conductivity times $\nabla T$. Written as fluxes through a face
normal to $x_a$, with $\mu=\nu\rho$ and the conductivity $\kappa\rho c_v$ in the default form,

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{(m_b)}_a &= -\nu\rho\,\big[\partial_av_b + \partial_bv_a - \tfrac23\delta_{ab}\nabla\cdot\mathbf v\big], \\
F^{(E)}_a &= \sum_b v_b\,F^{(m_b)}_a - \kappa\rho c_v\,\partial_aT ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-flux}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-viscosity-flux ch09_dropin_check.py [D4] -->

and the stage adds $-\Delta t\,\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$ to momentum and energy. With `dynamic: true`, $\nu\rho$ is
replaced by $\mu$ and $\kappa\rho c_v$ by the conductivity $\kappa$.

@eq-ch09-viscosity-flux is the face flux `momentum_flux` with its work and conduction terms in the energy row of
`DiffusionImpl::forward` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).

#### Discrete fluxes

On the face $i-\tfrac12$ normal to $x_1$, between cells $i-1$ and $i$, the code uses

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_1q\big|_{i-1/2} &= \frac{q_i-q_{i-1}}{\Delta x_1}, \\
\partial_bq\big|_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12\Big[\frac{q_{i,j+1}-q_{i,j-1}}{2\Delta x_b} + \frac{q_{i-1,j+1}-q_{i-1,j-1}}{2\Delta x_b}\Big], \\
\overline{q}_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12(q_{i-1}+q_i) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil ch09_dropin_check.py [D6] -->

the face-normal difference over the centre distance, the average of the two cell-centred tangential differences,
and the two-cell face average, in `face_normal_derivative`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_normal_derivative >}}), `centered_derivative`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp centered_derivative >}}) and `face_average`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_average >}}). The divergence $\nabla\cdot\mathbf v$ is formed with centred
differences in every cell, `div_vel`, and then face-averaged, `div_face`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}). The stress row $b=a$ is
$2\partial_av_a - \tfrac23\overline{\nabla\cdot\mathbf v}$; a row $b\ne a$ is $\partial_av_b + \partial_bv_a$, with
the second term dropped when direction $b$ is inactive. The viscous work uses the `face_average` of the velocity,
and the conductive term the face-normal temperature difference times the face coefficient of @sec-ch09-wallcoef.
The tendency subtracts $\Delta t$ times the `divergence` of the three flux arrays
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).

Three properties follow, and a line-by-line port of the module checks them:[^vis-c]

1. **Conservation.** Momentum and total energy change only by flux differences: the module's increment is
   `du -= dt * coord->divergence(...)`, the operator of @sec-ch02-laws, which forms each face product for both
   neighbours from identical operands, so the volume-weighted column sum telescopes to the outer faces (`[C4]`).
   In floating point each cell's increment carries three roundings, the face difference, the division by $V_i$ and
   the product with $\Delta t$, so on one active direction
   $\bigl\lvert\sum_iV_i\widehat{\Delta\mathbf U}_i+\Delta t([A\mathbf F]_{\mathrm{out}}-[A\mathbf F]_{\mathrm{in}})\bigr\rvert
   \le3\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\,\Delta t\sum_i\lvert\Delta_i[A\mathbf F]\rvert$ (check: at most 0.139 of it over 200 columns). The
   subtraction from `du` adds one rounding of each row's new value, $\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\lvert\Delta\mathbf U_i^{\mathrm{new}}\rvert$, relative
   to the whole increment of the cell.
2. **Dissipation.** The kinetic-energy part of the update is removed and the same amount is added to the internal
   energy through the work term; for a random shear the net internal-energy change is positive (`[C5]`).
3. **Accuracy.** For a transverse velocity the tendency is $\nu\rho$ times the three-point Laplacian to round-off,
   which decays a mode of wavelength $\lambda_w$ at
   $4\nu\sin^2\vartheta/h^2 = \nu(2\pi/\lambda_w)^2[1+O(\vartheta^2)]$, with $\vartheta=\pi h/\lambda_w$: second
   order (`[C2]`). The normal-stress row acts with the effective coefficient $\tfrac43\nu$, again second order; its
   stencil is wider because the divergence is a centred difference averaged to the face (`[C3]`).

**On a stretched $x_1$.** Two pieces of @eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil change, on $x_1$ only; $x_2$, $x_3$ and every
uniform $x_1$ keep the forms above. Write $h_{i-1}$ and $h_i$ for the widths of the cells below and above the face
$i-\tfrac12$ and $x_{1,i}$[^rg-7a33e3661515] [m] for the cell centres.

1. *The face mean.* `face_mean` takes $\overline q_{i-1/2}=(h_iq_{i-1}+h_{i-1}q_i)/(h_{i-1}+h_i)$.
2. *It is the face value of a linear profile.* For $q=a+bx_1$ the centre values are $q_{i-1}=q_f-bh_{i-1}/2$ and
   $q_i=q_f+bh_i/2$, with $q_f$ the value at the face. Then
   $h_iq_{i-1}+h_{i-1}q_i=(h_{i-1}+h_i)q_f+b(h_{i-1}h_i-h_ih_{i-1})/2=(h_{i-1}+h_i)q_f$, so $\overline q_{i-1/2}=q_f$.
   With $h_{i-1}=h_i$ it is $\tfrac12(q_{i-1}+q_i)$, the form above (`[C1]`).[^vis-x1]
3. *The centred difference.* `centered_derivative` along $x_1$ divides by the distance between the two centres,
   $(q_{i+1}-q_{i-1})/(x_{1,i+1}-x_{1,i-1})$. That is $b$ for $q=a+bx_1$ on any spacing, and the $2\Delta x_1$ form
   above on equal widths (`[C2]`).
4. *Where they enter.* The face mean gives the $x_1$ face divergence `div_face`, the face velocity of the viscous
   work, the face coefficient of the conduction (@sec-ch09-wallcoef), and, on an $x_1$ face, the mean of the two
   tangential differences of the cross term. The face-normal difference already divides by the centre distance.
5. *Hence* a velocity linear in $x_1$ has the exact stress on every interior $x_1$ face, and so does a
   conductivity linear in $x_1$ on its face coefficient.

[^vis-x1]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/stretched_x1_check.py`, output `stretched_x1_check.out`, lines
    `[C1]`–`[C4]`; a sympy and numpy port of `face_mean`, `centered_derivative`, `extrapolate_to_wall` and the
    cubed-sphere `weights` at snapy@68f4e066974ede87e4379285c4fba895b970b7f1, exact (`[C1]`–`[C3]`) and double
    (`[C4]`); Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0; the output matches the committed file.

[^vis-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/viscosity_check.py`, output `viscosity_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C8]`; a
    numpy port of `src/forcing/diffusion.cpp` at the pin, double precision.

#### Time-step bound

Forward Euler on the $n_{\mathrm{dim}}$-dimensional three-point Laplacian with coefficient $K_{\Delta t}$ amplifies the
checkerboard mode by $G = 1 - 4n_{\mathrm{dim}}K_{\Delta t}\Delta t/h^2$, so $|G|\le1$ requires

$$
\Delta t \le \frac{\Delta x_{\min}^2}{2n_{\mathrm{dim}}K_{\Delta t}},
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-dt}

with $K_{\Delta t}=\max(\nu\varsigma_{\max}^{\nu},\kappa\varsigma_{\max}^{\kappa})$ in the default form ($\varsigma_{\max}$ the
largest value of an $x_1$ profile of @sec-ch09-x1profile, 1 without one) and
$K_{\Delta t}=\max(\mu/\rho_{\min}, \kappa/(\rho c_v)_{\min})$ with `dynamic: true`, in `max_time_step`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::max_time_step >}}). At the bound $|G|=1$ exactly (`[C6]`). The
solver takes the minimum of @eq-ch09-viscosity-dt and the hyperbolic bound through `pdiffusion`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::max_time_step >}}) and then multiplies by the Courant factor `cfl`[^rg-b169a835b08c]
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step >}}), 0.9 by default in pyharp's integrator options,
so the diffusive step runs at `cfl` times its limit.

#### What `kappa_iso` diffuses

The energy row receives $\nabla\cdot(\kappa\rho c_v\nabla T)$. At fixed density the internal energy density is $\rho c_vT$,
so $\partial_tT = \kappa\nabla^2T$: `kappa_iso` is the thermal diffusivity of $T$. At fixed pressure the heat goes
into enthalpy, $\rho c_p\partial_tT = \kappa\rho c_v\nabla^2T$, and $T$ diffuses at $\kappa/\gamma$, 0.714286 of
$\kappa$ for $\gamma=1.4$ (`[C7]`). A run sits between the two, depending on how fast the pressure adjusts.

On a resting dry adiabat with $z=x_1$, the interior heating rate follows in four steps.

1. *The profile.* $\partial_zT=-\lvert g_1\rvert/c_{p,\mathrm d}$, uniform; $p\propto T^{c_{p,\mathrm d}/R_{\mathrm d}}$ and $\rho=p/(R_{\mathrm d}T)\propto T^{c_{v,\mathrm d}/R_{\mathrm d}}$.
2. *The flux divergence at fixed density.* $\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}\partial_tT=\partial_z(\kappa\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}\partial_zT)=\kappa c_{v,\mathrm d}\,\partial_z\rho\,\partial_zT$,
   because $\partial_z^2T=0$.
3. *The density gradient.* $\partial_z\rho/\rho=(c_{v,\mathrm d}/R_{\mathrm d})\,\partial_zT/T$.
4. *Hence* $\partial_tT=\kappa(c_{v,\mathrm d}/R_{\mathrm d})(\partial_zT)^2/T$, which is

$$
\partial_tT = \frac{\kappa \lvert g_1\rvert^2c_{v,\mathrm d}}{R_{\mathrm d}\,c_{p,\mathrm d}^2\,T},
$$ {#eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat ch09_dropin_check.py [D5] -->

$7.93\times10^{-7}$ $\mathrm{K\,s^{-1}}$ per unit $\kappa$ at $T=300$ $\mathrm{K}$ for dry air
($R_{\mathrm d}=287$, $c_{p,\mathrm d}=1004.5$ $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, $\lvert g_1\rvert=9.8$ $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$). The discrete operator
reproduces @eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat at second order: relative errors $1.85\times10^{-6}$, $4.63\times10^{-7}$
and $1.16\times10^{-7}$ at $n_1$ = 64, 128, 256 (`[C8]`).

*Exact and truncated.* Conservation of momentum and total energy is exact. The interior fluxes are second order;
at a reflecting $x_1$ wall the coefficient is second order (@sec-ch09-wallcoef) but the face-averaged divergence in
the normal stress is first order.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-viscosity-stencil shows the stencil of one $x_1$ face in two dimensions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-viscosity-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Stencil of the diffusive flux through the $x_1$ face $i-\\tfrac12$ (orange triangle on the orange face) on a 2-D Cartesian grid. Sky-blue circles are cell-centre primitives. The bluish-green arrow is the face-normal difference $\\partial_1 v$ across the face; the dashed black arrows are the centred $x_2$ differences in cells $i-1$ and $i$ whose average gives the cross term $\\partial_2 v_1$ of the shear stress. The face coefficient, $\\nu\\rho$ in $\\mathrm{Pa\\,s}$ or $\\kappa\\rho c_v$ in $\\mathrm{W\\,m^{-1}\\,K^{-1}}$, is the two-cell average except at a wall."
#| fig-alt: "Grid of four by three cells with cell centres as circles, one vertical face highlighted with a triangle, a horizontal double arrow across it and two vertical dashed double arrows in the cells on either side."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_viscosity_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Each face flux of @eq-ch09-viscosity-stencil reads the two cells across the face and, for the cross terms and the
divergence, their neighbours in the tangential directions: one ghost layer for conduction, two for viscosity (the
face average of a centred difference reaches two cells), hence the setup check $n_{\mathrm{ghost}}\ge2$. Ghosts are
filled by the boundary functions and the block exchange before the stage (@sec-ch11). Faces at a reflecting $x_1$
wall take the one-sided coefficient of @sec-ch09-wallcoef; every other face, including seams between blocks, takes
the two-cell average. With `temperature_inner` (or `temperature_outer`) $T_w>0$ at a wall named `reflecting_inner`
(`reflecting_outer`), the temperature difference across the wall face is replaced by the half-cell difference to the
wall, $\partial_1T\rvert_{\mathrm{wall}}=(T_c-T_w)/(x_{1,c}-x_{1,f})$, with $c$ the wall cell and $f$ the wall face, and
the wall-face coefficient is unchanged; the reflecting ghosts, which the hydrostatic balance reads, are not altered
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}). A linear profile between two such walls is then a
discrete equilibrium. The module runs in every Runge–Kutta stage, explicit, third in the forcing loop
(@sec-ch09-framework). Evidence for the orders: interior second order from `[C2]`, `[C3]` and `[C8]` (fitted slope
2.00 over three resolutions); the wall coefficient second order from @sec-ch09-wallcoef; the order of the full
operator at a wall through the solver is **not measured**.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The test deck's block ({{< code tests/test_diffusion.yaml >}}); viscosity needs `nghost: 2`:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamic`[^rg-e7230f85ba70].
```yaml
forcing:
  diffusion:
    nu_iso: 0.5        # m^2 s^-1, kinematic: times the face density
    kappa_iso: 0.25    # m^2 s^-1, thermal diffusivity: times the face rho c_v
    dynamic: false     # true: nu_iso is mu [Pa s], kappa_iso a conductivity [W m^-1 K^-1]
```

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *The legacy keys `K` and `type`*, with "DiffusionOptions: legacy 'K' and 'type' keys are unsupported; use
   'nu_iso' and 'kappa_iso'." ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}), and any other unknown key, by `check_keys` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).
2. *A coefficient that is not a finite number $\ge0$*, with "DiffusionOptions: KEY must be a finite number >= 0"
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}); *`dynamic` other than the literal `true` or `false`* ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).
3. *At setup, with a positive coefficient:* a grid other than Cartesian or the cubed sphere, "[Diffusion] Supported
   coordinates: cartesian, gnomonic-equiangle."; viscosity with fewer than two ghosts, "[Diffusion] Isotropic viscosity requires nghost >= 2.";
   conduction without a positive reference $c_v$ ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}). The stencil needs two ghosts, and the face
   coefficient needs $c_v$. *At setup, always:* a negative or non-finite wall temperature; a positive wall
   temperature on a Cartesian grid whose $x_1$ boundary on that side is not named `reflecting_inner` or
   `reflecting_outer`, "[Diffusion] Cartesian prescribed temperatures require reflecting x1 walls."; and
   `wall_velocity: no-slip` on a Cartesian grid, "[Diffusion] The no-slip wall option requires gnomonic-equiangle."
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}}).
4. *At run time*, a non-finite coefficient or a non-positive bound in `max_time_step` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-viscosity-flux** (`DiffusionImpl::forward`, per direction and velocity row):

```cpp
auto momentum_flux = options->dynamic()
                         ? -options->nu_iso() * stress
                         : -options->nu_iso() * rho_face * stress;
flux[IVX + ivar].index(face_index).copy_(momentum_flux);
flux[IPR].index(face_index) +=
    face_average(w[IVX + ivar], idir, face_start, face_end) *
    momentum_flux;
...
du -= dt * coord->divergence(fluxes[0], fluxes[1], fluxes[2]);
```

`stress` is the bracket of the first row (with `2. * stress - (2. / 3.) * div_face` on the diagonal, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}), so
`momentum_flux` is $F^{(m_b)}_a$; the `+=` line is the work $\sum_bv_bF^{(m_b)}_a$ of the second row, to which the heat flux
`- kappa_iso * coef * dtdn` is added ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}); the last line is $-\Delta t\,\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$.

   coefficients and a literal `true`/`false` for `dynamic`
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. `DiffusionImpl::reset` refuses a grid other than Cartesian or the cubed sphere when a coefficient is positive, the
   wall options of item 3, viscosity with fewer than two ghosts, and conduction without a positive reference $c_v$
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}});
   it then builds the $x_1$ profiles (@sec-ch09-x1profile).
3. `forward` hands a cubed-sphere block to `forward_cubed_sphere` (@sec-ch09-csdiffusion); on a Cartesian block it forms the cell divergence `div_vel` and `rho_cv`, then, per active direction, the face coefficient, the
   stress rows and their work, `momentum_flux`, and the heat flux from `dtdn`, with the wall value of `dtdn` replaced
   where a wall temperature is set ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).
4. It subtracts $\Delta t$ times the `divergence` of the three flux arrays
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).
5. `max_time_step` returns @eq-ch09-viscosity-dt ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::max_time_step >}});
   it throws on a non-finite coefficient or a non-positive bound.

: Tests of the isotropic viscosity and heat conduction. {#tbl-ch09-viscosity-tests}

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
**Evidence.** The check numbers come from the port named in the footnote. ctest cases: `test_diffusion.release`
and `test_stretched_x1_ref.release` pass at the pin.[^vis-ctest] A data figure of the sine-mode decay against $e^{-\nu t}$ from the ctest is **pending** the same run.
**Coverage.** The `DeviceTest` cases run on CPU in float32 and float64 and on CUDA in both when a device is present
(`tests/device_testing.hpp`). No multi-rank test of the module.
:::

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
This operator: Cartesian grids; the cubed sphere has its own (@sec-ch09-csdiffusion); other grids are refused. `kappa_iso` conducts on $T$, so a resting adiabat drifts. Immersed solids give a wrong face
coefficient by a factor of about 500 (@sec-ch09-wallcoef). No species or tracer diffusion.
:::

1. **Conduction on $T$.** A resting adiabatic column heats in the interior at @eq-ch09-viscosity-adiabat, and its
   wall cells, where the reflecting wall makes the conductive flux zero, depart from that rate. The module has no
   option to conduct on the potential temperature. The size of the wall drift through the solver is **not
   measured at the pin**: no committed deck runs a resting adiabat with conduction.
2. **Immersed solids** are read as fluid; see @sec-ch09-wallcoef.
3. **Wall normal stress.** At a reflecting $x_1$ wall the face-averaged divergence takes the cell value, an $O(h)$
   error in the kernel of the normal stress that the wall coefficient does not remove
   (`sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md` §5).
4. **Python setters** on `DiffusionOptions` bypass the YAML checks of step 1 of the walk-through; `reset` checks
   only the grid, the ghosts and $c_v$, so a negative coefficient set from Python is not refused there.
5. **Time step.** The bound uses the largest coefficient everywhere and the smallest cell width in any direction;
   it does not include the one-sided wall coefficient, which exceeds the two-cell average where the coefficient
   grows toward the wall. The default `cfl` of 0.9 leaves a margin; not measured at the pin.
6. **Untested combinations.** Diffusion with an implicit scheme, with sedimentation, or on several ranks is not run
   by any ctest listed here. See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
7. **Stretched $x_1$.** The weighted face mean and the centred difference are exact for profiles linear in $x_1$
   (Derivation); the order of the operator on a stretched $x_1$ is not measured, and conduction on a stretched
   Cartesian $x_1$ has no ctest of its own: the two `test_stretched_x1_ref` cases test the viscous terms.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-8453b354c365]: nu_iso — isotropic viscosity coefficient, interpreted according to dynamic

[^rg-c881080d630d]: kappa_iso — isotropic thermal transport coefficient, interpreted according to dynamic

[^rg-e72046dad063]: $\kappa$ — thermal diffusivity (or conductivity, stated); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L605-L639)

[^rg-6149e61825cb]: $\mu$, $\nu$ — dynamic and kinematic viscosity; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L595-L600)

[^rg-0527910bf49b]: $c_v, c_p$ — mixture specific heats **per unit total mass**, $c_v = \sum_n y_n c_{v,n}$ over dry air and every species [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; a chapter that needs the per-dry-mass form writes it out and says so

[^rg-ca98cd88ebb0]: $n_1, n_2, n_3$ — interior cells per block in each direction

[^rg-d9c30f993349]: $\tau$ — a relaxation time scale (named); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L102-L105)

[^rg-520b6f3f3b47]: $R_{\mathrm{d}}$, $R_n$ — specific gas constants of dry air and species $n$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L40-L43)

[^rg-2608062c5408]: $g_1, g_2, g_3$ — constant gravity components [m s$^{-2}$]; $g_1<0$ points to decreasing $x_1$

[^rg-90ec1bf7716b]: $\vartheta$ — local phase $\pi h/\lambda_w$ of a wave of wavelength $\lambda_w$ in a Fourier error estimate; notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-778cd93f3ca5]: $\lambda_w$ — a wavelength (named); notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-a3880ab85786]: temperature_inner — prescribed temperature of the inner x1 wall for heat conduction, in K; 0 (default) leaves the wall insulating

[^rg-900e6f628025]: temperature_outer — prescribed temperature of the outer x1 wall for heat conduction, in K; 0 (default) leaves the wall insulating

[^rg-78156b20840f]: wall_velocity — viscous condition at the radial walls on the cubed sphere: stress-free (default) or no-slip

[^rg-83f672728ba8]: $h_i$ — $x_1$ width of cell $i$, $x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i-1/2}$; written $\Delta x_1$ where the direction must be explicit

[^rg-7a33e3661515]: $x_{1,i}$ — cell volume centroid ($r_{c,i}$ on spherical-polar)

[^rg-b169a835b08c]: cfl — Courant-number limit for the time step

[^rg-e7230f85ba70]: dynamic — whether viscosity and heat transport use dynamic coefficients

[^rg-004bc25a0ec7]: nghost — number of ghost cells at each boundary
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
